description.narrative:
The development objectives of the Serving People, Improving Health Project for Ukraine are to improve the quality of health services in selected Oblasts, with special focus on primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular diseases and cancer, and to enhance efficiency of the health care system. The project is made up of three components. Under component 1 (Improving service delivery at the local level) the Project provides financing to selected Oblasts to carry out investment sub-projects aimed at prevention, early detection and treatment of cardiovascular diseases and cancer and at increasing efficiency of their health care delivery system (Oblast Sub-projects), including activities focused on improving primary health care, fighting cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) at the primary and secondary care levels, early cancer detection, and health delivery system rationalization. Component 2 (Strengthening Ministry of Health MoH governance) has been clustered around five thematic areas, with MoH as implementing agency: Payment System Reform, eHealth - Information
Systems Development, Public Health, Information and Communication, and Capacity Building. In addition, a decision has been made to bundle the resources of the five subcomponents into a common pool. Component 3 (Project implementation support, and monitoring and evalutation) supports the Project Consultancy Support Unit (PCSU) at national level, responsible for Project implementation support and technical assistance to the Oblasts. In addition, it would sponsor complementary data collection and analytical activities for monitoring results. Information from the existing Health Management Information System (HMIS) is complemented through audit of medical records on a sample basis, as well as through evidence based on specific, ad hoc household and facility surveys. In addition, the Project organizes learning events to educate and promote better use of evidence for policy.

The objectives of the Project are to: (i) improve efficiency and quality of health services, particularly for non-communicable diseases, in line with the health sector reforms; and (ii) prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19.

title.narrative: PDO Indicator 3: Improved quality management (prevention, early diagnosis and treatment) of CVDs at primary and secondary care measured as: a) reduction of hypertension-related hospitalization

comment.narrative: Overachieved, the target has been met (3.2 in 2022), however compared to 2021 the number of hospitalizations increased (2.3 in 2021, 4.94 in 2023). ???????Since February of 2022, the population has been in the state of constant psychological stress and exposed to negative socio-economic situations. Difficulties with logistics, such as transportation of medicines, were also added.

title.narrative: Share of health care providers benefiting from Project activities that that used the citizen feedback to enhance the quality of health services

comment.narrative: Overachieved. 580 facilities (63 percent) used public feedback to improve the quality of health services (timely response to a complaint or information request; placement of information on information boards/announcements/social networks; holding consultations with citizens, etc.).

title.narrative: PDO Indicator 2: Average in-patient length of stay in hospitals

comment.narrative: Achieved. Despite increased trauma cases since February of 2022 and a shift to outpatient care (reducing shorter stays), the Project effectively reduced ALOS by 3 days and decreased hospital beds, significantly improving system efficiency.

title.narrative: Health facilities constructed, renovated, and/or equipped (number)

comment.narrative: Overachieved. In total 34,592 people have been trained since 2015.

title.narrative: Percentage of all patients with acute stroke received thrombolytic therapy/mechanical thrombus removal
DLI 9: A specialized healthcare institution of national level has been contracted by NHSU and started performing services under the Program of Medical Guarantees
DLI 1: Hospitals from the capable network contracted by NHSU using case-based payments
DLI 2: PDO Indicator 1: Number of hospitals reprofiled or merged
DLI 7: PDO4: Number of hospital COVID-19 cases treated following agreed protocols and reimbursed by NHSU
DLI 8: Number of COVID-19 patients with complications attended by emergency medicine service following agreed protocols and reimbursed by NHSU

comment.narrative: Overachieved. The NHSU contracted emergency services centers in all regions of Ukraine for additional workload related to attending COVID patients.

title.narrative: DLI 8: Number of COVID-19 patients with complications attended by emergency medicine services following agreed protocols and reimbursed by NHSU
Improved patient care pathways for emergency stroke care and day surgeries developed and endorsed

comment.narrative: Overachieved. MOH has approved several standards and procedures to enhance emergency and stroke care. These include triage protocols for emergency departments, secondary stroke prevention, management of intracerebral hemorrhage, and addressing cognitive and psychoogical disorders post-stroke. Additionally, MOH, in collaboration with NHSU, has set forth requirements for day surgery services as part of the 2022 Medical Guarantees Program, updated for 2023. Furthermore, standards of care for ischemic stroke and regulations fr healthcare facility networks providing stroke care are being developed, alongside model regulations for specialized stroke departments and clinics, and an indicative list of equipment for stroke network departments.

title.narrative: DLI 3: NHSU monitors contracted providers and reviews records from contracted facilities
DLI 4: Percentage of all patients with acute stroke received thrombolytic therapy/ mechanical thrombus removal
Percentage of patients with acute stroke admitted to hospitals contracted by NHSU for provision of stroke care

comment.narrative: Overachieved. During 2023, the number of stroke patients admitted to all hospitals was 132,926. The number of stroke patients admitted to hospitals contracted by NHSU to provide medical care for stroke patients is 126,626 (of which: 61,720 are women n and 64,906 are men). Thus, 95 percent of stroke patients were admitted to hospitals with which NSHU concluded contracts for the provision of medical care for stroke patients.

title.narrative: DLI 3: NHSU monitors contracted providers and reviews records from contracted facilities
PDO Indicator 1: Number of hospitals reprofiled or merged

comment.narrative: Achieved. The WB health team has confirmed the achievement of the target in 100 hospitals. In total, there were 13 hospitals that were reprofiled, meaning that some hospital departments were closed down or restructured. Additionally, 87 hospitals were merged.

title.narrative: PDO 4: Number of hospital COVID-19 cases treated following agreed protocols and reimbursed by NHSU

comment.narrative: Overachieved. 52,630 patients (21,908 males and 30,722 females) were treated in intensive care units in 2021, target 10,000 patients.

title.narrative: DLI 5: Share of outpatient-based procedures and day surgeries
DLI 5: Share of outpatient-based procedures and day surgeries

comment.narrative: Overachieved. The baseline for DLI was identified for 2021 at 39.8 percent. MOH reported that during 2022 the share of outpatient-based procedures and day surgeries increased by 27 percent from the baseline.
